analysis:
The only visible change is in .github/workflows/ci.yml. It adds one step to the release-integrity job (head line 62-63): `python3 scripts/test_model_registry_workflow.py`, described as a loopback HTTP test of the model registry workflow. The head text shows no other changes; later lines shift by two. The job runs under workflow-level `permissions: contents: read` (line 8-9) on a hosted Linux runner. No secrets, release API key (A-005) or id-token access are visible in this step or this job. The step runs repository-supplied code on pull_request, the same as the existing neighbouring test steps. I see no new attack surface and no change to the canonical provider-side threat model (T-041, TB-011 and similar). The step makes no outbound or inbound network use beyond loopback as described.

Coverage limit: `.github/workflows/register-model.yml` is reported as modified, but only metadata was supplied (no patch, no base or head text, no mode change). That workflow plausibly handles model registration through the coordinator, which touches the A-005 release/registration key and the model weight hash registry (T-012, T-027). Its security effect cannot be judged. The next pass should read its diff for secret exposure, `pull_request_target` use, script injection through untrusted inputs, permissions widening, unpinned actions, and changes to how the coordinator is called. `scripts/test_model_registry_workflow.py` and any script it exercises were also not supplied.
